# @firefly0621/dsh-superpowers
English | 中文
## Summary
Bring the obra/superpowers workflow kernel and its fused extensions into a DeepSeek Harness profile
as one skill catalog plus a standing skill-first bootstrap. Use it when product sessions should move
from intent through plan, test, debug, review, and verification in a repeatable order. It is opt-in
and ships no harness peers.
## Package identity
Installable DeepSeek Harness plugin bundle that brings obra/superpowers into product sessions: a **3
5-skill** catalog split into core, advanced, product, and authoring bundles, adapted to dsh tooling,
plus a SessionStart-equivalent bootstrap. The default profile loads the 19-skill core bundle (`diag
nosing-superpowers` stays out until a deep dsh port).
[该节后续省略]
## What it restores
| Superpowers behavior | dsh realization |
| Skills library under `skills/*/SKILL.md` | `ctx.skills` provider `superpowers` (packaged `skills/`

directory, dsh-adapted) |
| SessionStart hook injecting `using-superpowers` | `system-prompt/assemb
le` section `skill:superpowers` with the same `<EXTREMELY_IMPORTANT>` framing (every non-subagent re

quest); `using-superpowers` is user-only in the skill catalog |
| Platform `references/*-tools.md` |

bundled `skills/using-superpowers/references/dsh-tools.md` appended inside that section |
| Subagen
t skip (`SUBAGENT-STOP`) | no full `using-superpowers` bootstrap when `session.header.origin === 'su

bagent'`; injects a short `skill:superpowers-worker` preamble instead |
| Model loads other skills o
n demand | existing `dsh-tool-skill` catalog + `skill` tool |
The skill bodies ship as dsh-adapted prose under `skills/` (no vendored source, no git submodule). F
oreign-harness tool names and platform references were rewritten for dsh, and the `superpowers:` ski
ll-name prefix was removed. The published tarball includes `skills/`, `assets/NOTICE.md`, and the of
fline scorer `scripts/score-skill-first.mjs`. NOTICE records obra/superpowers (`2ce8aa15`, v7.0.1),
mattpocock/skills (`5beb35b0`), addyosmani/agent-skills (`aeac41d4`), and bmad-code-org/BMAD-METHOD
(`61e01f82`, with trademark notice) as review pins.
Capabilities that overlap are fused into **one** owning skill. When an upstream source has material
that does not justify a second skill directory, it ships as a **reference pack** under the owner and
is loaded only at the step that needs it. The catalog therefore stays at 35 skills while the fused
behavior keeps growing.
## Version compatibility
This bundle declares `peerDependencies` on `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` packages. DSH checks those ranges ag
ainst the running runtime at install and profile startup; an incompatible pair is refused unless the
profile grants an exact `package@version` × `dsh-version` exemption. Source-workspace `workspace:*`
peers mean the matching DSH release; packed manifests substitute that exact version. See the plugin
manager's compatibility reference for `version-exemptions`, `allow-version`, and the crash/data-los
r's compatibility reference for `version-exemptions`, `allow-version`, and the crash/data-loss risk.
#### What the model sees
On every non-subagent request, `system-prompt/assemble` prepends section `skill:superpowers` whose t
ext is `buildBootstrapPreamble(...)`: the framing below, the body of the packaged `using-superpowers
` SKILL.md (frontmatter omitted), then `skills/using-superpowers/references/dsh-tools.md`. Agentless
assemblies omit the section. `session.header.origin === 'subagent'` gets `skill:superpowers-worker`
from `buildWorkerPreamble()` instead of the full bootstrap. Compaction cannot drop the guidance bec
ause it is reassembled with the system prompt each turn, not stored as a one-shot user message.
#### What the model sees
Indirectly through `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-skill`: every model-invocable Superpowers skill name/descr
iption in `<available_skills>`, and full bodies when loaded via `skill`.
## Known Limitations and Deferred Work
- No runtime invariant companion is published; skills are immutable packaged files and bootstrap is
a `system-prompt/assemble` listener with no independently observable durable event stream. Offline t
urn scoring lives in `scripts/score-skill-first.mjs` (first `tool/call` of each turn vs `skill`, plu
s same-turn `list_agents` counts after a `subagent` / `subagent_fork` dispatch); it does not enforce

behavior at runtime.
- **No upstream hook binary** — bootstrap is a Cordis `system-prompt/assemble`

listener, not `hooks/session-start`.
- **A complete persona replaces every section** — an agent who
se composition registers a `complete` persona (agent presets) suppresses all prompt sections, includ

ing `skill:superpowers` and `skill:superpowers-worker`, for that agent.
- **Packaged preamble must a
void `{{...}}` prompt-variable syntax** — `loadBootstrapPreamble` rejects a complete `{{name}}` grou
p at plugin apply (mirrors skill-always-apply); a custom `skillsRoot` that introduces one fails loud

before the first turn.
- **Cross-harness reference content is removed** — foreign platform tool ref
s, Anthropic skill-authoring guides, and harness-specific testing examples are omitted; `dsh-tools.m

d` is the sole platform adapter and must stay deep enough for SDD wait/resume/model routing.
- **Ups
tream sync is manual** — no vendored submodule; re-porting means diffing against the recorded commit
s and re-applying the dsh adaptation. A local `superpowers/` checkout is for comparison only; keep i

t outside this repository.
- **`diagnosing-superpowers` out of catalog** — obra v6.4.1+ ships a sess
ion-diagnosis skill that depends on foreign harness transcript paths and a large prompt/template tre
e; a shallow port would mislead. A deep dsh adaptation is a separate feature, not open sync debt. Pa

ckaged catalog length is **35**; default core is **19**.
- **Optional bundles are opt-in** — `advanc
ed`, `product`, and `authoring` skills are packaged but not loaded by default. A profile that needs
product discovery or skill authoring must add the bundle name to config; the plugin does not infer i

t from the task.
